note: Generated from the annexes of specs/100-specstride by contracts/tools/generate.py. The annex stands where the two differ.

controls.Content: The control plane is outside the proposer's write scope. Approval is a signed record, verified on `resume`
Containment levels C0 to C3 as a capability of a harness adapter. The strongest available is the default; C0 is an opt-in in user configuration
One point of redaction, which fails closed. Content is captured whenever traces are on, so this point carries the risk, and its patterns are widened and tested with planted canaries before a release
Project configuration may narrow a run and never widen it
Text from outside the runtime is framed as data everywhere

threats.Threat: A verdict line planted in phase evidence or in a grounded file
threats.Control: A nonce of 64 bits per call; the verdict is parsed only from the reply, as a full line, with exactly one match; MALFORMED is the safe failure

threats.Threat: The proposer forges approval state
threats.Control: R-1; the signed approval record bound to verdict, evidence hash, verification result and tree fingerprint; `resume` verifies

threats.Threat: Text persuades the critic to approve
threats.Control: The verification gate runs before the critic and cannot be overridden by it; critic diversity; R-5; a critic without tools

threats.Threat: Phase evidence imitates a banner of the runtime
threats.Control: Random boundary tokens per call on every section; the boundary pattern is escaped in untrusted text; facts of the runtime stand before untrusted text

threats.Threat: The nonce is written before the call returns
threats.Control: Never stored or exported before the return; afterwards only its hash

threats.Threat: Evidence makes the critic reply malformed until the run halts
threats.Control: The safe failure is kept; the halt at the MALFORMED limit is a stop that is not retryable (`critic_unavailable`), shown as an attention item; it is not a member of the blocked reasons and emits no `blocked` event

threats.Threat: A proposer with all tools acts on injected instructions
threats.Control: R-2; the environment allow-list; the runtime never asserts a sandbox

threats.Threat: An injected critic reply reaches the next phase attempt through feedback
threats.Control: Feedback is framed as data; only criterion ids and the text after them are taken, with a cap; the verdict line is removed

threats.Threat: Repository text makes the host model alter the consumer's comment
threats.Control: The comment is passed verbatim and stored with its hash before any repository text is printed; the digest shows it

threats.Threat: A comment is read as permission to skip a check
threats.Control: Enforcement lives in the runtime; no flag switches off a launch check, the terms gate or a budget cap

threats.Threat: The host model reports a run wrongly
threats.Control: The digest is produced by the runtime from events and printed verbatim

threats.Threat: Output of the product injects the host session
threats.Control: Default output is terse; untrusted text is never echoed, only named

threats.Threat: Project configuration declares a harness, a critic, a command or an endpoint
A discovered harness claims falsely that it qualifies as critic
threats.Control: Only a mode that the runtime enforces and proves qualifies; the pick is announced and recorded; identity of the provider comes from the endpoint

threats.Threat: An executable shadows a harness on the search path
threats.Control: Resolved to an absolute path at launch; paths inside the workspace are refused

threats.Threat: An endpoint points at an attacker
threats.Control: Endpoints from user scope only; a secret is bound to its host; unencrypted endpoints are refused except loopback

threats.Threat: A stream imitates terminal records or cost figures
threats.Control: Only the harness's own framing is parsed; caps per line

threats.Threat: A harness with unknown cost spends without being counted
threats.Control: Budgets by wall clock and count of passes; the doctor says that spend cannot be measured

threats.Threat: The proposer edits what a check reads
threats.Control: The check manifest is frozen and hashed at launch; the protected set is fingerprinted before and after every check; a change is a fact for the critic

threats.Threat: The proposer weakens the tests it is measured by
threats.Control: Changes to existing tests and suppression markers are facts for the critic

threats.Threat: A check runs repository code with the runtime's environment
threats.Control: A scrubbed environment, no provider key, containment, no write access to the control plane, a time limit

threats.Threat: An inner result is taken for a verdict
threats.Control: A loop layer holds no writer of the phase gate; the tripwire

threats.Threat: Repair history reaches the critic through files of the proposer
threats.Control: Records of the runtime stay in the control plane; grounding refuses state paths; such files are claims

threats.Threat: The proposer overwrites the result the critic will see
threats.Control: The result is written by the runtime into the control plane and handed over by the runtime

threats.Threat: A check with huge output or without end
threats.Control: Output cap, time limit, end of the process group, the first-failure predicate

threats.Threat: A process record points at an unrelated process
threats.Control: The process registry is in the control plane; a signal only when pid, start time and run token match

threats.Threat: A stale or planted lock blocks every run
threats.Control: Liveness backed by the kernel; reclaim by rename; the doctor reports a lock without a live holder

threats.Threat: The proposer writes a stop request, a snapshot or a state file
threats.Control: R-1; replayed settings are validated against the schema and the trust classes again

threats.Threat: Other users of the machine read the state
threats.Control: Permissions for the owner only; the doctor checks

threats.Threat: A link or a path leaves its root
threats.Control: Real paths must stay inside their root; links in the control plane are refused

threats.Threat: The event file is edited or cut
threats.Control: The event file is in the control plane; `seq` has no gaps; the ledger is chained and signed

threats.Threat: Content leaves the machine on spans
threats.Control: R-3; capture can be switched off; the doctor shows the endpoint and whether capture is on

threats.Threat: A secret printed by a tool reaches records
threats.Control: R-3; exact-match removal of resolved secrets; the scan before a commit

threats.Threat: The proposer inherits the whole environment
threats.Control: The environment allow-list per harness adapter

threats.Threat: A secret is written inline or on a command line
threats.Control: References only; passed by environment or standard input

threats.Threat: A telemetry endpoint is set by the project or by the proposer
threats.Control: Telemetry endpoints are widening keys

threats.Threat: An exporter blocks or fails
threats.Control: Sinks never break the loop

threats.Threat: A viewer in a browser: requests from other origins
threats.Control: No component of Wave 1 opens a network listener. The read model renders nothing; a later viewer is read-only, bound to loopback, with a token per session
threats.Owner: 129 for the read model (Wave 1); the viewer is Wave 2

threats.Threat: A viewer in a browser: other local users
threats.Control: No component of Wave 1 opens a network listener. The read model renders nothing; a later viewer is read-only, bound to loopback, with a token per session
threats.Owner: 129 for the read model (Wave 1); the viewer is Wave 2

threats.Threat: A viewer in a browser: script in rendered text
threats.Control: No component of Wave 1 opens a network listener. The read model renders nothing; a later viewer is read-only, bound to loopback, with a token per session
threats.Owner: 129 for the read model (Wave 1); the viewer is Wave 2

threats.Threat: A viewer in a browser: exported pages
threats.Control: No component of Wave 1 opens a network listener. The read model renders nothing; a later viewer is read-only, bound to loopback, with a token per session
threats.Owner: 129 for the read model (Wave 1); the viewer is Wave 2

threats.Threat: A viewer in a browser: a listener that outlives the run
threats.Control: No component of Wave 1 opens a network listener. The read model renders nothing; a later viewer is read-only, bound to loopback, with a token per session
threats.Owner: 129 for the read model (Wave 1); the viewer is Wave 2

threats.Threat: A malicious version is published
threats.Control: Publishing from the build on a protected branch, with attestation

threats.Threat: A dependency is compromised
threats.Control: Few dependencies, exact versions, no install script, nothing compiled at install

threats.Threat: An impostor package or plugin
threats.Control: The documentation and the host package name the exact package; the host package verifies the protocol integer

threats.Threat: The host package installs the CLI silently
threats.Control: It detects, reports and prints the command

threats.Threat: The launch bundle is edited between rendering and launch
threats.Control: The hash of the launch bundle and of the launcher are verified at launch and at every relaunch

threats.Threat: A critic with read-only tools reads the project by itself
threats.Control: A read-only sandbox with the network off; the proposer's notebook, handoff and outbox moved out; the withheld paths denied; the grounding snapshot and the nonce as before. Repository text can still reach this critic without passing the snapshot: a residual risk the owner accepted

threats.Threat: Several workers on one phase
threats.Control: Containment C2 by default; a repository of its own per worker; the store unwritable by workers; composition of audited, disjoint deltas; the merge check and the full verification gate on the workspace; neutral integrity kinds
